content.content:
commit 317b51f2ad0894b4e7eea33e41938806551c3892
Author: Andy Wilkinson <awilkinson@pivotal.io>
Date:   Wed Mar 7 09:57:16 2018 +0000

    Make ApplicationContextRequestMatcher and subclasses thread-safe
    
    Previously, when performing lazy initialisation of the context,
    ApplicationContextRequestMatcher assigned the context field before it
    called initialized. The context being non-null is used as the signal
    that it’s ok to call a subclass’s matches method. If one thread checks
    for a non-null context in between the field being assigned and
    initialized being called on another thread, matches will be called
    before the subclass is ready.
    
    This commit closes the window for the race condition by only assigning
    the context field once the subclass’s initialized method has been
    called.
    
    There is a secondary problem in each of the subclasses. Due to the use
    of double-checked locking in ApplicationContextRequestMatcher, it’s
    possible for a subclass’s matches method to be called by a thread that
    has not synchronised on the context lock that’s held when initialized
    is called and the delegate field is assigned. This means that the
    value assigned to the field may not be visible to that thread.
    
    This commit declares the delegate field of each
    ApplicationContextRequestMatcher subclass as volatile to ensure that,
    following initialisation, its value is guaranteed to be visible to
    all threads.
    
    Closes gh-12380

diff --git a/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/security/servlet/ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java b/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/security/servlet/ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java
index 84441b3eb4..11d29b1d25 100644
--- a/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/security/servlet/ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java
+++ b/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/security/servlet/ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java
@@ -69,8 +69,9 @@ public abstract class ApplicationContextRequestMatcher<C> implements RequestMatc
 		if (this.context == null) {
 			synchronized (this.contextLock) {
 				if (this.context == null) {
-					this.context = createContext(request);
-					initialized(this.context);
+					Supplier<C> createdContext = createContext(request);
+					initialized(createdContext);
+					this.context = createdContext;
 				}
 			}
 		}

delta.text: confirms it. Commit `5938ca78b6` replaced the correct double-checked locking (which held a lock while `initialized()`

ran, ensuring the second thread waited) with `AtomicBoolean.compareAndSet(false, true)` — the second thread's `compareAndSet` immediately returns `false` and proceeds straight to `matches(request, context)` without wai
ting for the first thread's `initialized(context)` call to complete. That race is exactly what `f03ca7e175` fixes by switching to

`synchronized` double-checked locking again.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 5938ca78b6e6bd86364

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java` with `git log --follow` and reviewed each commit that
touched the `matches`/`initialized` synchronization logic, since the fix commit's whole purpose is to prevent `matches` from running before `initialized` completes under concurrency

.

**(2) Specific change:** In `5938ca78b6` ("Fix request matcher management context support"), the author replaced the previous thread-safe implementation:
antees that `initialized(context)` is called exactly once — it does **not** make a second concurrent caller wait for that call to finish. Thread B

's `compareAndSet` fails immediately (since Thread A already set it to `true`) and Thread B proceeds directly to `matches(request, context)`, potentially before Thread A's `initialized(context)` has returned. This reintroduces the exact race
condition that an earlier commit (`317b51f2ad`, "Make ApplicationContextRequestMatcher and

subclasses thread-safe") had deliberately closed using synchronized double-checked locking.

**(3) Evidence:** The fix commit `f03ca7e175` reverts precisely this pattern — removing `

AtomicBoolean` and reintroducing a `synchronized` block with double-checked locking (`volatile boolean initialized` + `initializeLock`), so that a second thread blocks on the lock until the first thread's
`initialized()` call and flag update complete. The added regression test (`matchesWhenConcurrentlyCalledWaitsForInitialize`) directly exercises two concurrent threads calling
`matches`, asserting `initialized` has been set before `matches` proceeds — which fails under the `compareAndSet` logic introduced in `5938
ca78b6` but passes with the synchronized fix. This strongly confirms `5938ca78b6` is the bug-introducing commit.
